# shiki-loader

> A drop-in, framework-agnostic browser script that automatically syntax-highlights `<pre><code>` blocks using Shiki. It bundles into a single self-contained JS file with embedded CSS, loads Shiki from esm.sh at runtime, and adds language labels and copy-to-clipboard buttons to every code block. Configured entirely via URL query parameters on the script tag.

The loader is browser-only with zero Node.js dependencies. Shiki is imported from esm.sh at runtime, not bundled. CSS is inlined into the JS bundle at build time via a placeholder replacement step. The script must be loaded with `type="module"`. `window.ShikiLoader.highlight()` re-runs highlighting for content added later and skips blocks that are already highlighted.

The repository contains two parts: the standalone loader (`src/shiki-loader/`) and a Next.js demo app (`src/app/`) deployed to GitHub Pages.

## Getting Started

<doc title="README" path="./README.md">
# shiki-loader

[![Deploy to GitHub Pages](https://github.com/vespaiach/shiki-loader/actions/workflows/deploy-pages.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/vespaiach/shiki-loader/actions/workflows/deploy-pages.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Shiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/Powered%20by-Shiki-ff69b4)](https://shiki.style/)

A drop-in browser script that automatically syntax-highlights `<pre><code>` blocks using [Shiki](https://shiki.style/). Nothing to install and no build step for consumers, framework-agnostic. Shiki itself is loaded from [esm.sh](https://esm.sh/) at runtime.

**[Live Demo](https://vespaiach.github.io/shiki-loader/)**

## Features

- Automatic detection and highlighting of all `<pre><code>` blocks on the page
- 60+ bundled themes, with a light/dark pair that follows `prefers-color-scheme` live
- All [Shiki bundled languages](https://shiki.style/languages) supported out of the box
- Language label and copy-to-clipboard button on every code block
- Self-contained single script — CSS is embedded, Shiki is loaded from [esm.sh](https://esm.sh/) at runtime
- Works with any static site, CMS, blog, or HTML page

## Quick Start

Add a single `<script>` tag to your HTML:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vespaiach/shiki-loader@v2.1.0/public/shiki-loader.js" type="module"></script>
```

That's it. All code blocks with a language class will be highlighted on page load.

### Specify Themes

```html
<!-- Single theme -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vespaiach/shiki-loader@v2.1.0/public/shiki-loader.js?theme=github-dark" type="module"></script>

<!-- Light and dark mode themes -->
<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vespaiach/shiki-loader@v2.1.0/public/shiki-loader.js?theme=github-light&dark-theme=github-dark"
  type="module"
></script>
```

### Code Block Format

The loader highlights any `<code>` element inside a `<pre>` that has a `language-*` or `lang-*` class:

```html
<pre><code class="language-typescript">
const greeting: string = 'Hello, world!';
console.log(greeting);
</code></pre>
```

## Configuration

The loader is configured entirely via URL query parameters on the script `src`.

| Parameter    | Values                       | Default          | Description                                      |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `theme`      | Any bundled Shiki theme name | `material-theme` | Theme used in light mode (and dark if no dark-theme) |
| `dark-theme` | Any bundled Shiki theme name | _(none)_         | Theme used when system prefers dark mode         |

When `dark-theme` is set, each block is rendered with both themes and CSS switches between them via `prefers-color-scheme`, so the colors follow the system setting live, without a reload. Without `dark-theme`, `theme` is always used.

Language names are case-insensitive. `text`, `plaintext`, `txt` and `plain` get the wrapper and copy button without highlighting. Blocks with an unsupported language, or no language class, are left untouched.

### Highlighting Content Added Later

The loader runs once when the page loads. For content inserted afterwards (SPA navigation, lazy-loaded comments), call:

```js
await window.ShikiLoader.highlight(container); // or highlight() for the whole document
```

Blocks that are already highlighted are skipped, so it is safe to call repeatedly.

### Customizing the Look

The loader's styles are inserted at the top of `<head>`, so your own stylesheet overrides them without `!important`:

```css
/* Hide the window dots */
.shiki-loader-mockup-code:before { display: none; }

/* Scroll long lines instead of wrapping them */
.shiki-loader-mockup-code pre { white-space: pre; display: block; }

/* Hide the language label */
.shiki-loader-language-label { display: none; }
```

Any `id`, classes and other attributes on the original `<pre>` are carried over to the highlighted block.

### Supported Themes

Popular themes include:

| Light                       | Dark                         |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `github-light`              | `github-dark`                |
| `one-light`                 | `one-dark-pro`               |
| `catppuccin-latte`          | `catppuccin-mocha`           |
| `material-theme-lighter`    | `material-theme-darker`      |
| `rose-pine-dawn`            | `rose-pine`                  |
| `solarized-light`           | `solarized-dark`             |
| `everforest-light`          | `everforest-dark`            |
| `min-light`                 | `nord`                       |

See [src/shiki-loader/themes.ts](src/shiki-loader/themes.ts) for the full list of 60+ themes.

## Self-Hosting

Build the loader locally and serve `shiki-loader.js` from your own domain:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vespaiach/shiki-loader.git
cd shiki-loader
bun install
bun run build:lib
```

The output file is `public/shiki-loader.js`. Copy it to your project's static assets and reference it in your HTML:

```html
<script src="/assets/shiki-loader.js?theme=dracula" type="module"></script>
```

## How It Works

1. The script reads `theme` and `dark-theme` from its own URL (`import.meta.url`), so it must be loaded with `type="module"`
2. On DOM ready, it injects its embedded CSS once
3. Finds all `<pre><code>` elements with a `language-*` or `lang-*` class
4. Highlights each block using Shiki (loaded from esm.sh at runtime), with both themes when `dark-theme` is set
5. Wraps each block with a language label and copy-to-clipboard button
6. Exposes `window.ShikiLoader.highlight()` for content added later

## Development

### Prerequisites

- [Bun](https://bun.sh/) 1.0+

### Setup

```bash
bun install
bun run type-check    # Verify TypeScript setup
bun run build:lib     # Build the loader
```

### Scripts

| Command             | Purpose                                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `bun run dev`       | Start Next.js dev server at localhost:3000              |
| `bun run build:lib` | Build standalone loader to `public/shiki-loader.js`    |
| `bun run build`     | Build Next.js static site                              |
| `bun run start`     | Run production server                                  |
| `bun run lint`      | Lint with Biome                                        |
| `bun run format`    | Format with Biome                                      |
| `bun run type-check`| TypeScript type-check (no emit)                        |
| `bun test`          | Run tests                                              |

### Project Structure

```
src/
├── shiki-loader/          # The standalone loader (framework-agnostic)
│   ├── index.ts           # Entry point — DOM detection and highlighting
│   ├── transformer.ts     # Wraps highlighted blocks with UI (label + copy button)
│   ├── utils.ts           # URL param parsing, CSS injection, clipboard handling
│   ├── loader.css         # Styles embedded into the bundle at build time
│   └── themes.ts          # List of supported Shiki themes
├── app/                   # Next.js demo app
│   ├── layout.tsx         # Root layout (Tailwind + DaisyUI)
│   ├── page.tsx           # Home page
│   ├── about/page.tsx     # About page
│   └── _components/       # Demo-specific components
└── components/            # Shared UI components (Select, icons)
```

### Build Pipeline

`bun run build:lib` does:
1. Bundles `src/shiki-loader/index.ts` with Bun (`--target browser --bundle --minify`)
2. Runs `scripts/embed-loader-css.ts` to inline `loader.css` into the JS bundle
3. Outputs final self-contained script to `public/shiki-loader.js`

## Loader Architecture

<doc title="Entry Point — index.ts" path="./src/shiki-loader/index.ts">
// @ts-expect-error for simplicity, we can ignore type errors in this loader since it's meant to be used as a standalone script
import { bundledLanguages, codeToHtml } from "https://esm.sh/shiki@3.0.0";
import createShikiLoaderTransformer from "./transformer";
import { generateStyles, handleCopyButtonClick, readSearchParams } from "./utils";

// Shiki's plain-text languages are not part of bundledLanguages.
const languages = new Set([...Object.keys(bundledLanguages), "text", "plaintext", "txt", "plain"]);
const { theme, darkTheme } = readSearchParams(import.meta.url);
let hasRun = false;

async function highlight(root: ParentNode = document) {
  if (!hasRun) {
    hasRun = true;
    // Prepended so the host page's own CSS can override the loader's styles.
    document.head.prepend(generateStyles());
  }

  const highlightTasks = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll("pre code")).map(async (codeBlock) => {
    const element = codeBlock as HTMLElement;
    const parent = element.parentElement;
    if (!parent) return;

    // Extract language from class (e.g., language-js)
    const langClass = Array.from(element.classList).find((c) => /^(language|lang)-/.test(c));
    if (!langClass) return;

    const lang = langClass.replace(/^(language|lang)-/, "").toLowerCase();
    if (!languages.has(lang)) {
      console.warn("Unsupported language:", lang);
      return;
    }

    try {
      // Markup like <code>\n...\n</code> would otherwise render blank first and last lines.
      const code = (element.textContent || "").replace(/^\n|\n$/g, "");
      const html = await codeToHtml(code, {
        lang,
        // With two themes Shiki emits both sets of colors and loader.css switches between them.
        ...(darkTheme ? { themes: { light: theme, dark: darkTheme } } : { theme }),
        transformers: [createShikiLoaderTransformer(lang)],
      });

      const tempDiv = document.createElement("div");
      tempDiv.innerHTML = html;
      const newPre = tempDiv.firstElementChild as HTMLElement | null;

      if (newPre) {
        for (const { name, value } of Array.from(parent.attributes)) {
          if (name !== "class" && name !== "style") newPre.setAttribute(name, value);
        }
        newPre.classList.add(...Array.from(parent.classList), langClass);
        newPre
          .querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("button[data-target='copy']")
          ?.addEventListener("click", handleCopyButtonClick);
        parent.replaceWith(newPre);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(`Failed to highlight code block with language "${lang}":`, err);
    }
  });

  await Promise.allSettled(highlightTasks);
}

// Lets pages highlight content added after load: ShikiLoader.highlight(container)
Object.assign(window, { ShikiLoader: { highlight } });

// Side effect to automatically highlight on load
// Works both for scripts present at initial load and for
// scripts injected dynamically after DOMContentLoaded.
if (document.readyState === "loading") {
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
    void highlight();
  });
} else {
  void highlight();
}
</doc>

<doc title="Utilities — utils.ts" path="./src/shiki-loader/utils.ts">
// @ts-expect-error for simplicity, we can ignore type errors in this loader since it's meant to be used as a standalone script
import { bundledThemes } from "https://esm.sh/shiki@3.0.0";

export interface LoaderInputs {
  theme: string;
  darkTheme?: string;
}

const LOADER_CSS = "/* LOADER_CSS placeholder - this will be replaced with the contents of loader.css */";
const themes = new Set(Object.keys(bundledThemes));

export function generateStyles() {
  const style = document.createElement("style");
  style.textContent = LOADER_CSS;
  return style;
}

export function readSearchParams(src: string): LoaderInputs {
  const config: LoaderInputs = { theme: "material-theme" };
  const params = new URL(src).searchParams;

  const themeParam = params.get("theme") ?? "";
  if (themes.has(themeParam)) {
    config.theme = themeParam;
  }

  const darkThemeParam = params.get("dark-theme") ?? "";
  if (themes.has(darkThemeParam)) {
    config.darkTheme = darkThemeParam;
  }

  return config;
}

const tooltipResetTimers = new WeakMap<HTMLElement, number>();

export async function handleCopyButtonClick(event: MouseEvent) {
  const button = event.currentTarget as HTMLButtonElement | null;
  if (!button) return;

  const tooltip = button.closest(".shiki-loader-tooltip") as HTMLElement | null;
  const container = button.closest(".shiki-loader-mockup-code") as HTMLElement | null;

  if (!container) return;

  const codeElement = container.querySelector("pre code") as HTMLElement | null;
  const code = codeElement?.textContent ?? "";

  if (!code) return;

  try {
    if (navigator.clipboard?.writeText) {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(code);
    } else {
      const textarea = document.createElement("textarea");
      textarea.value = code;
      textarea.style.position = "fixed";
      textarea.style.opacity = "0";
      document.body.appendChild(textarea);
      textarea.focus();
      textarea.select();
      try {
        document.execCommand("copy");
      } finally {
        document.body.removeChild(textarea);
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("Failed to copy code to clipboard:", err);
    return;
  }

  if (!tooltip) return;

  const previousTimeout = tooltipResetTimers.get(tooltip);
  if (previousTimeout !== undefined) {
    window.clearTimeout(previousTimeout);
  }

  tooltip.setAttribute("data-tip", "Copied");

  const timeoutId = window.setTimeout(() => {
    tooltip.setAttribute("data-tip", "Copy");
    tooltipResetTimers.delete(tooltip);
  }, 2000);

  tooltipResetTimers.set(tooltip, timeoutId);
}
</doc>

.shiki-loader-mockup-code {
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  direction: ltr;
  padding-block: 1.25rem;
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  position: relative;
  overflow: visible;
}
.shiki-loader-mockup-code:before {
  content: "";
  opacity: 0.3;
  border-radius: 3.40282e38px;
  width: 0.75rem;
  height: 0.75rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  display: block;
  box-shadow:
    1.4em 0,
    2.8em 0,
    4.2em 0;
}
.shiki-loader-mockup-code pre {
  padding-right: 1.25rem;
  padding-left: 2ch;
  overflow: auto;
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  display: inline-block;
}
.shiki-loader-tooltip {
  position: absolute;
  right: 0.75rem;
  top: 0.75rem;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  z-index: 10;
  --tt-off: calc(100% + 0.5rem);
  --tt-tail: calc(100% + 1px + 0.25rem);
  --tw-content: attr(data-tip);
}
.shiki-loader-copy-button {
  cursor: pointer;
  width: 1.5rem;
  height: 1.5rem;
  background: transparent;
  border: none;
  padding: 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
}
.shiki-loader-tooltip:hover::before {
  opacity: 1;
  --tt-pos: 0rem;
}
/* Separate rule: a browser without :has() would otherwise drop the hover rule too. */
.shiki-loader-tooltip:has(:focus-visible)::before {
  opacity: 1;
  --tt-pos: 0rem;
}
.shiki-loader-tooltip::before {
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
  text-align: center;
  white-space: normal;
  max-width: 20rem;
  opacity: 0;
  color: oklch(92% 0.004 286.32);
  background-color: oklch(14% 0.005 285.823);
  pointer-events: none;
  z-index: 2;
  content: var(--tw-content);
  width: max-content;
  padding-block: 0.25rem;
  padding-inline: 0.5rem;
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  line-height: 1.25;
  position: absolute;
  transform: translate(calc(var(--tt-pos, 0.25rem) - 0.25rem)) translateY(-50%);
  inset: 50% var(--tt-off) auto auto;
}
.shiki-loader-language-label {
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  top: 1.05rem;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  opacity: 0.8;
}

/* Dual themes: Shiki inlines the light colors and exposes the dark ones as --shiki-dark* variables.
   !important is required to beat those inline light colors. */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  .shiki-loader-mockup-code.shiki-themes,
  .shiki-loader-mockup-code.shiki-themes pre,
  .shiki-loader-mockup-code.shiki-themes span {
    color: var(--shiki-dark) !important;
    background-color: var(--shiki-dark-bg) !important;
    font-style: var(--shiki-dark-font-style) !important;
    font-weight: var(--shiki-dark-font-weight) !important;
    text-decoration: var(--shiki-dark-text-decoration) !important;
  }
}
</doc>

## Development

<doc title="CLAUDE.md — Development Guide" path="./CLAUDE.md">
## Build & Development Workflow

### Building the Loader

Command: `bun run build:lib`

This:
1. Bundles `src/shiki-loader/index.ts` with Bun (`--target browser --bundle --minify`)
2. Runs `scripts/embed-loader-css.ts`, which inlines `loader.css` into the JS bundle via a placeholder in `utils.ts`
3. Outputs the final script to `public/shiki-loader.js`

The loader script is entirely self-contained: no external CSS files, no external dependencies (Shiki is imported from esm.sh at runtime).

### Running the Demo App Locally

`bun run dev` — Next.js app runs at localhost:3000.

### Static Build for GitHub Pages

`bun run build` then `bun run start` — exports to static HTML with `basePath` and `assetPrefix` set for `/shiki-loader/` on GitHub Pages.

### Pre-Merge Checklist

```bash
bun run lint          # Check for style/lint violations
bun run type-check    # Verify TypeScript compiles
bun run build:lib     # Build the loader
bun run build         # Build the demo app
bun run test          # Run all tests
```

## Key Development Guidelines

- Keep the loader framework-agnostic — no React/Next.js imports in `src/shiki-loader/`
- Browser-only: guard `document`, `window`, `navigator.clipboard` access
- `hasRun` ensures the CSS is injected once; `highlight()` can be re-run via `window.ShikiLoader.highlight(root?)`
- CSS is embedded; no external stylesheets
- Edit `loader.css` directly, then `bun run build:lib` to embed
- New URL parameters go in `readSearchParams()` in `utils.ts`
- TypeScript target is ES2017 for broad browser compatibility
- Biome enforces 2-space indent, 110-char line width, double quotes
- `public/shiki-loader.js` is checked in (jsDelivr serves it); rebuild and commit it when the loader changes
</doc>

## Optional

<doc title="Copilot Instructions" path="./.github/copilot-instructions.md">
# Copilot Instructions for shiki-loader

## Project Overview

This repo contains:

- A **browser-only Shiki loader** in src/shiki-loader that can be built into a single script (public/shiki-loader.js) and dropped into any HTML page.
- A **Next.js demo app** (app directory) used to showcase and manually test the loader and its themes.

All logic is client-side; there is no Node runtime dependency for the loader itself.

## Shiki Loader Architecture

- Entry point: src/shiki-loader/index.ts — Imports Shiki from esm.sh, auto-runs on DOM ready, finds `pre code` blocks, and replaces them with highlighted HTML. Exposes `window.ShikiLoader.highlight(root?)` for content added later. Must be loaded with `type="module"`.
- Transformer: src/shiki-loader/transformer.ts — Wraps each Shiki `<pre>` in a container with language label and copy-to-clipboard button.
- Utilities: src/shiki-loader/utils.ts — `readSearchParams(src)` reads theme params from the script URL (`import.meta.url`), `generateStyles()` injects CSS, `handleCopyButtonClick()` copies the code and shows "Copied" only on success.
- Themes: src/shiki-loader/themes.ts — Source of truth for supported Shiki theme names.

## Language Detection

- Languages from Shiki `bundledLanguages` via `Object.keys(bundledLanguages)`, plus `text`, `plaintext`, `txt` and `plain`.
- Accepts `language-xxx` or `lang-xxx` classes on code elements; names are case-insensitive.
- A block naming an unsupported language logs a warning and is skipped; a block with no language class is skipped silently.

## Theme Selection & Dark Mode

- `readSearchParams(src)` returns `{ theme, darkTheme }` with default `theme = "material-theme"`.
- darkTheme set → Shiki renders both themes and loader.css switches them with a `prefers-color-scheme` media query, live. Otherwise → theme is always used.
- Unknown values fall back to `material-theme`.

## Build & Development

- Loader build: `bun run build:lib` — bundles, minifies, embeds CSS via placeholder.
- Dev server: `bun run dev`
- Lint: `bun run lint` (Biome), Format: `bun run format`, Type-check: `bun run type-check`, Tests: `bun test`

## Implementation Guidelines

- Keep loader framework-agnostic — no React/Next imports in src/shiki-loader.
- Browser-only: guard document/window/navigator.clipboard access.
- Keep `highlight()` safe to call repeatedly; `hasRun` only guards CSS injection.
- Edit loader.css for styles, rely on embed script to inline.
- New themes: verify Shiki supports it, update themes.ts.
- New config: add URL parameters in readSearchParams(), keep backward-compatible.
</doc>
